warning: Seeds below are published test values and must never sign anything real.
signing: Ed25519 over canonical_json directly. No domain prefix: schema_version inside the envelope separates this format.
authenticator_note: Cases marked authenticator=valid must pass cryptographic verification so the semantic rule under test is actually reached. Cases marked invalid fail verification itself.
row_columns_note: Where a case carries row_columns, those are the values stored in the row's own columns, overriding the equally-named envelope fields. The envelope is what was signed; the columns are what a reader queries.

rejection_cases.name: sequence_num is not the expected successor
rejection_cases.note: Signed consistently, so the signature verifies and the sequence rule is reached.

rejection_cases.name: prev_event_hash does not chain to the previous row
rejection_cases.note: Signed consistently; the link is what fails.

rejection_cases.name: event_hash disagrees with canonical_json
rejection_cases.note: Envelope and signature are untouched; the stored hash is wrong.

rejection_cases.name: signature does not verify under the device key
rejection_cases.note: Signed by a different key over the correct bytes.

rejection_cases.name: row column seq disagrees with the signed envelope
rejection_cases.note: The row sits at the right chain position and its stored seq is correct, so the sequence rule passes. The signed envelope says something else, which is the disagreement rule 5 exists to catch.

rejection_cases.name: row column prev_event_hash disagrees with the signed envelope
rejection_cases.note: The row's stored link is correct, so the chain rule passes. The signed envelope carries a different predecessor, which is rule 6.

rejection_cases.name: row column event_id disagrees with the signed envelope
rejection_cases.note: The envelope and its signature verify. The row's stored column contradicts them, which is what rules 5 to 10 exist to catch.

rejection_cases.name: row column event_type disagrees with the signed envelope
rejection_cases.note: The envelope and its signature verify. The row's stored column contradicts them, which is what rules 5 to 10 exist to catch.

rejection_cases.name: row column device_id disagrees with the signed envelope
rejection_cases.note: The envelope and its signature verify. The row's stored column contradicts them, which is what rules 5 to 10 exist to catch.

rejection_cases.name: row column emitted_at_ms disagrees with the signed envelope
rejection_cases.note: The envelope and its signature verify. The row's stored column contradicts them, which is what rules 5 to 10 exist to catch.

rejection_cases.name: schema_version is verity.v1
rejection_cases.note: A v1 row fails here rather than being reinterpreted as v2.

rejection_cases.name: payload_json disagrees with the envelope payload
rejection_cases.note: The envelope is authentic; the separately stored payload column is not.

rejection_cases.name: envelope carries a field this contract does not define
rejection_cases.note: Signed consistently, so rule 13 is reached rather than the signature failing first.

rejection_cases.name: runtime_action payload carries no authority
rejection_cases.note: Every other rule holds. The payload names a runtime action and declares no licensing authority, which is the absence rule 14 exists to catch.

rejection_cases.name: authority is not an object
rejection_cases.note: The field is present, so rule 14 passes. It is a string, so no kind can be selected and no field rule is reachable.

rejection_cases.name: authority kind is outside the vocabulary
rejection_cases.note: A well-formed object carrying a well-formed proposal_id. Only the kind is unrecognised, so no field rule is reachable.

rejection_cases.name: a field the kind requires is absent
rejection_cases.note: The kind is recognised and every present field is valid; profile_id is missing, which is rule 17 and not rule 18.

rejection_cases.name: a required field fails its grammar
rejection_cases.note: The field set is exact and the kind recognised. profile_id fails its owning grammar on case alone, which is the narrowest way to break only rule 18.

rejection_cases.name: authority carries a field its kind does not permit
rejection_cases.note: proposal_id is well formed, so rule 18 passes and the only fault is the zone_id this kind does not permit.

chain_context_note: Each rejection case publishes the chain position it was presented at, so a verifier can evaluate the sequence and link rules without inferring them. row_columns are the values stored in the row's own columns; the envelope is what was signed. Rules 5 to 10 are the cases where those two disagree.
conformance_note: A conforming verifier must find each case violating exactly the rule it names and no other. A case that violates a second rule would pass a naive check while never exercising the rule it was written for.
